ca_charlotte_s_web_area.blurb: A small cluster of sandstone boulder problems inside the Brickyard, a compact bouldering zone in the hills above Santa Barbara. The thirteen problems cover a wide range: a few easy warm-ups, a solid middle run of V2 to V5, and four harder lines from V7 up to V10. Expect cracks, an arete and some traverses rather than one single style. The Brickyard as a whole is shady, dense with problems and the rock is generally good quality, though the zone is not large, so this makes a handy short session rather than a full-day destination.

ca_magic_school_bus_area.blurb: A roadside bouldering pocket in Culp Valley, the desert boulder field between Borrego Springs and Ranchita in San Diego County, at roughly 3,500 feet. It holds thirteen problems and leans easy: about half are V0 or easier, with a middle group at V2 to V4 and a single V5 at the top end. Several lines are roofs and tall problems, and one of the V3 problems is flagged as a spicy, high-consequence line. It sits further along the dirt road than the main Culp zones. Winter and the cool shoulder months suit desert bouldering best.

ca_high_tension_towers.blurb: A short crag in the Central Gorge of the Owens River Gorge near Bishop, just upstream of the Banana Belt wall. Thirteen routes, mostly bolted lines with a few trad options, on welded tuff: a couple of easy pitches, then a heavy concentration of 5.10 climbs and a pair of 5.11s. Routes run up to about 100 feet. The wall catches less sun than its neighbour and has fewer standout pitches, so it is quieter, and the overhead power lines hum constantly, giving the place an industrial feel. Mornings and late afternoons are the comfortable times to climb here.
ca_high_tension_towers.approach: Walk to the Banana Belt, then follow the trail upstream a few hundred feet toward the electrical tower.

ca_penny_royal_arches.blurb: A south-facing granodiorite wall in Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite, at about 8,770 feet and tucked behind Pywiack Dome, marked by a large arch. All thirteen routes are trad, from an easy slab to one very hard 5.13 line, with most of the climbing between 5.7 and 5.11. Expect slab and friction moves with sparse protection on the easier terrain, and a quiet day, since the crag draws far fewer people than the famous domes nearby. The approach is an easy off-trail walk through open trees. Summer and early autumn are the usual window at this elevation.

ca_h_rubble_row.blurb: A sector of Riverside Quarry in the Inland Empire, where the cliff meets the big pile of dirt and broken rock that fills much of the quarry floor. It has thirteen single-pitch sport climbs on granite, roughly 80 to 120 feet long. Most are 5.10, with a couple of easier 5.8 and 5.9 lines, one 5.11 and a single 5.13 for the strong. Loose debris at the base means careful footwork. Bring a standard sport rack and quickdraws; some tape helps on the rough rock.

ca_gainsborough_boulders.blurb: A small training boulder spot in the Los Angeles area, on a hill known locally as Tarantula Hill. The sandstone is short but overhanging, and the main wall is about twenty yards long and sits in shade nearly all day. Thirteen problems fall almost entirely between VB and V3, so it suits beginners and anyone wanting a quick local session more than a trip. Holds can break when the rock is damp, so wait out any rain before pulling on.

ca_eliminator_boulder.blurb: One of the six boulder groups at The Knobs, beside Tioga Road in Tuolumne Meadows at about 8,400 feet. The granodiorite here hosts thirteen problems from V0 up to V7, a spread that includes a few famous classics, a traverse and some sit-start variations. Most of the harder lines sit in the V3 to V7 range, so strong boulderers will find plenty to try while easier warm-ups exist too. The walk from the roadside pullout is only a few minutes uphill. The Knobs is among the more popular bouldering stops in Tuolumne, so plan on company in peak season.
ca_eliminator_boulder.approach: A few minutes' walk uphill from the roadside parking, bearing slightly to the right.

ca_more_water_less_power_boulder.blurb: A quality rhyolite boulder in the Central Happiness area of the Happy Boulders, the sheltered boulder-filled wash north of Bishop in the Eastern Sierra. Thirteen problems, most of them easy to moderate: a handful from VB to V1, several V2 and V3 lines, and two V5 problems at the top, including a long traverse and a low, powerful line. Many of the easier problems are low-angle overhangs with friendly holds, so it works well for mixed groups. The canyon holds warmth on cold days, which suits the cooler months.
